summary: Augsburg Airport (AGB/EDMA) is a regional airport located approximately 7 kilometers northeast of Augsburg city center in Bavaria, Germany. Originally established as a military airfield, it now primarily serves general aviation, business flights, flight training, and occasional charter operations. It is one of the few remaining operational airfields in the greater Munich area.
faqs:
Q: Does Augsburg Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No, the airport does not offer regular scheduled commercial service. It primarily handles general aviation, private jets, flight training, and occasional charter flights.

Q: How far is Augsburg Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is located about 7 km northeast of central Augsburg, typically a 15-20 minute drive by car.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features a terminal building, fuel services, aircraft maintenance facilities, flight schools, and hangar space for private and business aircraft.

Q: Is there a control tower at Augsburg Airport?
A: Yes, the airport is tower-controlled during operating hours, ensuring safe coordination of arriving and departing traffic.
transport_tips: The most convenient way to reach Augsburg Airport is by car via the B2 federal road, with ample parking available near the terminal. Taxi services and ride-shares from Augsburg city center are readily available and typically cost around 20-30 euros. Public bus connections are limited, so arranging private transport in advance is recommended for time-sensitive travel.
local_tip: If you have time before or after your flight, the airfield's edge offers a pleasant spot for plane spotting, especially during weekends when flight schools are most active and you can watch a variety of training aircraft taking off and landing.
